lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Verify that the LinkedIn address is the actual public profile URL and that all contact items are clickable in the PDF.
items.because: Recruiters need reliable, frictionless contact links.

items.says: Replace `example.com` if it appears on the real résumé.
items.because: Recruiters need reliable contact links.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: Neither is standard or helpful on a U.S. résumé, and both can introduce discrimination concerns.

items.says: Make the MBA’s completion status unambiguous.
items.because: Recruiters care primarily about completion status and graduation timing.

items.says: Consider showing only the graduation date if space is needed.
items.because: Recruiters care primarily about completion status and graduation timing.

items.says: Add GPA, honors, concentration, or relevant leadership only if strong and useful for target roles.
Make the date treatment and degree formatting consistent with the MBA entry.
items.because: Consistency improves readability and professionalism.

items.says: Standardize date ranges with the same dash style and month format.
items.because: Formatting inconsistencies make the document look less polished.

items.says: Clarify whether 35% is a relative or percentage-point improvement.
items.because: The result lacks enough context to assess credibility.

items.says: Add the measurement period, sample size, or experimental method.
items.because: The result lacks enough context to assess credibility.

items.says: Verify or narrow the claim that the change was for all merchants.
items.because: The claim may be too broad if the change reached only a subset.

items.says: Avoid implying causation unless the design supports it.
items.because: The current claim lacks enough context to assess credibility.

items.says: Add a post-launch business or customer result if available.
items.because: Shipping early is an execution metric, while adoption or resolution speed would better show product impact.

items.says: Clarify the plan used to measure early shipment and whether you influenced the acceleration.
Keep punctuation consistent around lists.
Change “analysed” to consistent U.S. spelling.
items.because: The résumé mixes American context with British forms.

items.says: Format the monetary figure compactly and identify its currency if needed.
Clarify whether the loss figure was annualized, estimated, or directly observed.
items.because: The estimate could raise questions.

items.says: Tighten the connection between the analysis and roadmap decision without overstating sole ownership.
items.because: The bullet compresses several ideas.

items.says: Clarify whether closing tickets meant fully resolving them.
items.because: Resolution is more meaningful than administrative closure.

items.says: Give the starting and ending queue sizes if possible.
items.because: Absolute baselines make the improvement more credible.

items.says: Consider removing “over the summer.”
items.because: The internship dates already establish the period.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not support a causal measurement of the redesign.
items.because: Self-selecting merchants may differ systematically, creating selection bias.

items.says: Identify the comparison as observational and explain any controls, or remove the bullet.
items.because: Opt-in and non-opt-in merchants may differ systematically.

items.says: Do not present the comparison as A/B testing.
items.because: Self-selection makes the comparison vulnerable to selection bias.

items.says: Report a result rather than only the measurement activity.
items.because: The bullet reports an activity without a result.

items.says: Move the onboarding outcome to the first or second Harbor bullet.
items.because: Product recruiters prioritize customer and business impact.

items.says: Clarify your individual ownership relative to the team.
items.because: Ownership should be defensible.

items.says: State how the reduction was measured and whether it was sustained.
items.because: Measurement should be defensible.

items.says: Ensure “single verification step” does not oversimplify compliance or risk requirements.
Reduce Harbor Payments to four or five bullets.
items.because: Business outcomes should take priority over process details.

items.says: Order Harbor bullets with onboarding and checkout first, then chargeback discovery and dispute self-service, and ticket triage last or omitted.
items.because: Product recruiters prioritize customer and business impact over internal operating cadence.

items.says: The claimed reduction in late deliveries is a reporting-definition change, not an operational improvement.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments did not make any deliveries less late.

items.says: Add the period over which the pick-error reduction was measured.
items.because: Measurement context will make the result more credible.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction was sustained and whether 30% is relative.
items.because: Measurement context will make the result more credible.

items.says: “Prepares” is inconsistent with the past-tense role.
items.because: The bullet contains a grammatical error.

items.says: Spell out S&OP at first use unless every target employer will recognize it.
Add an outcome of the review or forecast work if available.
items.because: The bullet describes routine responsibilities rather than an achievement.

items.says: Explain how the annual driver-hour savings were calculated or validated.
items.because: The savings estimate should be defensible.

items.says: Add a business result such as cost, utilization, delivery performance, or mileage if available.
Use “Present” only if you remain actively involved; otherwise give the end date.
items.because: Current involvement should be accurate.

items.says: Clarify whether “Product Lead” was an official role or a descriptive title.
items.because: Role ownership should be accurate.

items.says: Clarify what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: “Launched to” may indicate potential reach rather than adoption.

items.says: Clarify whether the food figure was tracked or estimated, and label an estimate.
items.because: The food-impact claim needs a clear basis.

items.says: Use U.S. English and measurement conventions instead of “tonnes.”
items.because: The résumé mixes American context with British forms.

items.says: Do not imply that interviews alone proved why students missed pickup windows.
items.because: Interviews identify reported reasons rather than establish causation.

items.says: Specify the period over which weekly active users increased.
Do not attribute the entire user increase to reminders without credible analysis.
items.because: The causal claim is stronger than the evidence described.

items.says: Clarify the definition of weekly active user if it is not obvious.
Explain what “staff cover shifts” means.
items.because: Recruiters outside the organization may not understand the term.

items.says: Add the measurement period and clarify whether the 95% fill rate was sustained.
State what the working sessions produced or remove the bullet.
items.because: Holding meetings is an activity, not an accomplishment.

items.says: Replace the passive construction to clarify your and the team’s contributions.
items.because: The bullet obscures ownership.

items.says: Quantify the form reduction and its effect if available.
items.because: The bullet provides no measured impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the changes were piloted, adopted, or fully implemented.
The merchant-onboarding result is duplicated from Harbor Payments and unrelated to the hospital practicum.
items.because: It is a visible editing error.

items.says: Remove “A/B testing” unless you have designed, run, or analyzed controlled experiments.
items.because: The opt-in onboarding comparison is not evidence of A/B testing, and unsupported skills invite probing questions.

items.says: Ensure each listed product skill can be supported with specific examples.
items.because: Unsupported skills invite probing questions.

items.says: List Jira, Amplitude, and Excel only if you can explain how you used them and at what depth.
items.because: A skills section should be a credible inventory.

items.says: Aim for a one-page résumé.
items.because: That length suits the experience level and MBA profile.
